input_signals.name: Accrual Share of Net Investment
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), ADD(ABS(SUB(ib, oancf)), ABS(SUB(capx, dp)))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose investment mix is dominated by positive accruals rather than capital expenditure net of depreciation should earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded ratio distinguishes accounting-based growth from additions to productive fixed capital without multiplying two standalone anomaly ranks. Negative accruals occupy the opposite tail, while substantial net capex moderates the signal even when accruals are positive, yielding an economically ordered spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), add( abs( sub( ib, oancf ) ), abs( sub( capx, dp ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Inventory-Exposed Accrual Reversal
input_signals.hypothesis: Positive accruals should reverse more strongly at firms with greater balance-sheet exposure to inventory.
input_signals.reasoning: Inventory intensity measures the stock of assets exposed to obsolescence, markdowns, and demand-estimation errors, rather than reusing inventory growth as a mechanical component of current accruals. Because inventory intensity is ordinarily nonnegative, it continuously amplifies positive accrual risk without creating a doubly-low nonmonotonic tail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( invt, at ), ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Net Intangible Capitalization
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-asset accumulation that exceeds recognized depreciation and amortization should predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This construction measures a capitalization-versus-expensing gap rather than applying another balance-sheet exposure multiplier to total accruals. A high value indicates that recognized intangible assets are accumulating faster than broad noncash asset costs are being charged through earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( delta( intan, 1 ), dpc ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Cumulative Accrual Investment Imbalance
input_signals.expression: RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), ADD(ABS(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3)), ABS(TS_SUM(SUB(capx, dp), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with persistently positive cumulative accruals relative to cumulative net fixed investment should earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The strongest archived signal compares annual accruals with net investment, but one-year measurement can be distorted by project timing and working-capital reversals. Aggregating dollar flows before forming the bounded share identifies sustained accounting-over-productive growth and may stabilize both regression slopes and portfolio membership.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( ts_sum( sub( ib, oancf ), 3 ), add( abs( ts_sum( sub( ib, oancf ), 3 ) ), abs( ts_sum( sub( capx, dp ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Capitalization Allocation
input_signals.hypothesis: Asset formation concentrated in recognized intangible growth rather than tangible capex or depreciation and amortization charges should predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal treats dpc correctly as broad depreciation and amortization rather than claiming that a small dpc-minus-dp reconciliation residual isolates amortization. Its bounded composition compares intangible accumulation with tangible investment and contemporaneous noncash expensing, directly distinguishing capitalization-heavy growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( intan, 1 ), add( abs( delta( intan, 1 ) ), add( abs( capx ), abs( dpc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill-Heavy Purchase Allocation
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill creation that is large relative to cash acquisition spending and recognized depreciation and amortization should predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash acquisition spending enters only as a scale benchmark, so large acquirers are no longer mechanically assigned favorable signals through a negative purchase-price residual. High values instead identify transactions dominated by non-amortizing goodwill and purchase-accounting valuation rather than observable cash investment or expense recognition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( delta( gdwl, 1 ), add( abs( delta( gdwl, 1 ) ), add( abs( aqc ), abs( dpc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Noncash PPE Formation
input_signals.hypothesis: Net PPE growth that exceeds the amount explained by capex less depreciation and amortization should predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The residual isolates tangible-asset formation not supported by reported cash capital expenditure, including acquisition consolidation, revaluation, and other nonorganic balance-sheet changes. Unlike substituting net PPE growth for capex minus depreciation, this construction explicitly uses their accounting reconciliation gap as the signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( delta( ppent, 1 ), sub( capx, dp ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Capital Spending Charge Imbalance
input_signals.hypothesis: A large mismatch between current capital spending and recognized depreciation and amortization should predict lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Large positive gaps identify aggressive expansion exposed to the investment anomaly, while large negative gaps identify erosion of the capital base or unusually heavy write-offs. Treating both directions as an imbalance resolves the conflicting low-versus-high depreciation conditioning stories instead of imposing another total-accrual multiplier.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( abs( sub( capx, dp ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Positive Noncash PPE Additions
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(ADD(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ppent, 1), SUB(capx, dp)), LAG(at, 1)), ABS(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ppent, 1), SUB(capx, dp)), LAG(at, 1)))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Positive PPE additions unexplained by capex net of depreciation should predict lower returns, while unexplained PPE reductions should not be treated as the opposite opportunity.
input_signals.reasoning: The signed reconciliation residual had a strong negative Fama-MacBeth slope but a sharply positive portfolio alpha, suggesting that its negative tail represents economically different events such as disposals or restructurings. The one-sided construction retains noncash asset additions while mapping reductions to neutral, directly addressing that portfolio asymmetry.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( add( ratio( sub( delta( ppent, 1 ), sub( capx, dp ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ), abs( ratio( sub( delta( ppent, 1 ), sub( capx, dp ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Internal Funding Coverage
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ABS(capx), ABS(aqc))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating cash flow covers capital expenditure and acquisition investment should earn higher subsequent returns than firms with large internal funding deficits.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded ratio directly compares realized operating cash with two observable forms of real investment, distinguishing cash-supported expansion from growth requiring external finance or accounting earnings. Because FF5 controls for profitability and investment separately, any surviving alpha would reflect their funding interaction rather than either level alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), add( abs( oancf ), add( abs( capx ), abs( aqc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Material Internal Funding Coverage
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), LAG(at, 1)), RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ABS(capx), ABS(aqc))))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Material capital and acquisition investment funded by operating cash flow should predict higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The unweighted internal-funding ratio produced the strongest aligned evidence in the latest generation but can assign extreme scores to cash-rich firms making little investment. Multiplying by total investment intensity makes low-investment firms neutral and isolates the return difference between internally funded and externally dependent expansion at economically meaningful investment levels.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), lag( at, 1 ) ), ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), add( abs( oancf ), add( abs( capx ), abs( aqc ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Accrual Share of Total Investment
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), ADD(ABS(SUB(ib, oancf)), ABS(ADD(SUB(capx, dp), aqc))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Positive accruals that dominate both organic net investment and acquisition spending should predict lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The strongest archived accounting-versus-investment signal omits acquisitive investment, potentially classifying acquisition-intensive firms as having little real investment. Adding cash acquisitions to replacement-adjusted capex tests whether the accrual reversal depends on accounting growth relative to the firm's full observable investment program.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), add( abs( sub( ib, oancf ) ), abs( add( sub( capx, dp ), aqc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Multi-Year Internal Funding Capacity
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(capx, aqc), 3), LAG(at, 3)), RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(oancf, 3), TS_SUM(ADD(capx, aqc), 3)), ADD(ABS(TS_SUM(oancf, 3)), ABS(TS_SUM(ADD(capx, aqc), 3))))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained material investment covered by cumulative operating cash flow should predict higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Multi-year aggregation matches operating cash generation with the investment program over a project cycle, reducing distortions from annual payment and acquisition timing. Scaling by cumulative investment intensity prevents persistent cash generators with little actual investment from dominating the favorable portfolio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( ts_sum( add( capx, aqc ), 3 ), lag( at, 3 ) ), ratio( sub( ts_sum( oancf, 3 ), ts_sum( add( capx, aqc ), 3 ) ), add( abs( ts_sum( oancf, 3 ) ), abs( ts_sum( add( capx, aqc ), 3 ) ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Earnings-Cash Investment Funding Illusion
input_signals.expression: SUB(RATIO(SUB(ib, ADD(capx, aqc)), ADD(ABS(ib), ABS(ADD(capx, aqc)))), RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(ADD(capx, aqc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose investment appears funded by reported income but not by operating cash flow should earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The difference directly measures how accrual accounting changes the apparent funding capacity for the same observable investment program. It avoids attributing negative operating cash flow to nonexistent equity or debt issuance and remains continuous across firms with different financing choices.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ratio( sub( ib, add( capx, aqc ) ), add( abs( ib ), abs( add( capx, aqc ) ) ) ), ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), add( abs( oancf ), abs( add( capx, aqc ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Material Organic Funding Coverage
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(capx, LAG(at, 1)), RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(capx)))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Material organic capital expenditure covered by operating cash flow should predict higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Focusing on capex removes the zero mass and thin acquirer subsample that undermined the acquisition-specific construction. Capex intensity keeps firms with negligible investment near neutral, while the coverage ratio distinguishes internally funded productive spending from cash-deficit expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( capx, lag( at, 1 ) ), ratio( sub( oancf, capx ), add( abs( oancf ), abs( capx ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Downside Internal Funding Resilience
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(MA(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), LAG(at, 1)), 3), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ABS(capx), ABS(aqc)))), 3)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms sustaining material investment without an internal funding deficit even in their weakest recent year should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The minimum coverage state captures downside funding resilience rather than average cumulative coverage, which can hide a single severe cash shortfall. Multiplication by average investment intensity prevents low-investment cash generators from dominating the favorable portfolio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ma( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 3 ), ts_min( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), add( abs( oancf ), add( abs( capx ), abs( aqc ) ) ) ), 3 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Cash Validation of Residual Asset Growth
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(oancf, SUB(DELTA(at, 1), ADD(capx, aqc))), ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(SUB(DELTA(at, 1), ADD(capx, aqc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Asset growth not attributable to capital expenditure or acquisitions should predict higher returns only when it is validated by operating cash generation.
input_signals.reasoning: Subtracting observable real investment from total asset growth isolates balance-sheet expansion more likely to reflect working assets, reclassification, or other accounting formation. The bounded comparison rewards cash generation relative to that residual growth without turning fully covered firms into a pure gross-investment sort or using an unstable asset-light capital denominator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( oancf, sub( delta( at, 1 ), add( capx, aqc ) ) ), add( abs( oancf ), abs( sub( delta( at, 1 ), add( capx, aqc ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual Share versus Gross Capacity Formation
input_signals.hypothesis: Positive accruals that dominate gross tangible-capacity formation should predict lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross PPE growth measures formation of installed productive capacity before depreciation, making it economically distinct from capex minus depreciation and from free-cash-flow profitability. The bounded share directly contrasts accounting earnings growth with observable real capital formation while avoiding denominator explosions for asset-light firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), add( abs( sub( ib, oancf ) ), abs( delta( ppegt, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Common-Scale Earnings Cash Funding Gap
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), ADD(ABS(ib), ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(ADD(capx, aqc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Reported income exceeding operating cash flow should predict lower returns when the gap is large relative to both funding measures and the observable investment program.
input_signals.reasoning: A single common denominator makes the earnings-cash difference directly comparable and avoids subtracting two coverage ratios normalized by different scales. Capital expenditure and acquisitions enter as an economic benchmark that attenuates a given accrual gap when it accompanies a substantial real investment program, rather than multiplying accruals by investment intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), add( abs( ib ), add( abs( oancf ), abs( add( capx, aqc ) ) ) ) )
